docs.summary: Moves a character along the navmesh using crowd simulation: give it a [`Destination`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~Destination) (or call [`SetDestination`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~SetDestination)) and it steers there, avoiding other agents. The agent joins the scene's crowd when a navmesh for its [`AgentTypeId`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~AgentTypeId) is available and writes its position back to the Transform each LateUpdate (disable [`UpdatePosition`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~UpdatePosition) to drive a Rigidbody or CharacterController from [`DesiredVelocity`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~DesiredVelocity) yourself).
Writing this re-places the agent on its new type's crowd, keeping its destination. One agent type per navmesh, so this is a move between crowds rather than a parameter.
The raw crowd agent, while registered. Advanced use.
True while the agent is registered on a navmesh crowd.
The query filter this agent paths with: its area mask, agent type and area costs.
Set or get the movement target. Setting it requests a new path.
True while a requested path is still being computed by the crowd's path queue.
True once the agent has reached its destination, until a new destination or path is set, the path is reset, or the agent is warped.
Raised once when the agent reaches its destination.
True when the agent has a path it is following.
Status of the current path.
True while the agent is traversing an off-mesh link (the crowd animates the hop; traversal is always automatic).
The off-mesh traversal in progress (Valid false while walking normally). Resolves back to the [`NavMeshLink`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink) component via the id stamped at bake.
Current velocity of the agent in the crowd simulation.

The velocity the agent wants (path steering before avoidance/acceleration limits). Drive a Rigidbody or CharacterController from this when [`UpdatePosition`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~UpdatePosition) is off.
The agent's position in the crowd simulation (before [`BaseOffset`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~BaseOffset)).
The next corner the agent is steering toward.

Distance to the end of the current path along its corners. Infinity while no path is available. When the path's visible corner window doesn't yet reach the destination this is a lower bound, which is enough for arrival checks against [`StoppingDistance`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~StoppingDistance).

Stop (true) or resume (false) movement. The path is kept while stopped, so resuming carries on along it rather than replanning. [`SetDestination`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~SetDestination) while stopped plans the route but does NOT clear the stopped state — movement resumes only when this is set back to false.

Two things a stopped agent still does: an off-mesh hop already under way finishes (the crowd animates it to the far side rather than stranding it mid-air), and a corridor that cannot reach its target is re-planned about once a second until it can.
Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.

Push the steering properties (speed, radius, avoidance, area mask and costs) into the live crowd agent. Every setter that feeds them calls this, as do an inspector edit and [`SetAreaCost`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~SetAreaCost), so it is only needed by hand after mutating the cost table reached through [`Filter`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.Filter).

docs.summary: Override the path cost of an area for this agent, for explicit queries and crowd steering both. Clamped to at least 1 (see [`SetAreaCost`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAreaCosts~SetAreaCost)); to prefer an area, raise the other areas' costs instead.
The path cost this agent pays in an area: its own override, or the project default.
Remove this agent's cost overrides, falling back to the project costs.

Request a path to `target`. Returns false when the agent is not on a navmesh or the target cannot be mapped onto it. A stopped agent ([`IsStopped`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~IsStopped)) plans the route but stays halted until resumed: IsStopped is a pause flag that survives new destinations.

Follow a pre-calculated path, steering along the route it describes rather than re-planning one to its endpoint. The path must come from [`CalculatePath`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~CalculatePath) (or [`CalculatePath`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~CalculatePath)) and start where the agent is standing; the crowd still re-plans later if the navmesh invalidates it.
docs.returns: False if the path is unusable, does not begin at the agent's current polygon, or crosses more polygons than a crowd agent's corridor holds.

Teleport the agent (and Transform) to a position on the navmesh. Keeps the current destination.

Displace the agent by a world-space offset, constrained to the navmesh — the per-frame API for driving an agent yourself. Slides the path corridor along, keeping the path, boundary cache and neighbour set; use [`Warp`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~Warp) to jump somewhere unrelated, which rebuilds all of that.

members.name: SamplePathPosition
members.signature: public bool SamplePathPosition(NavMeshAreaMask areaMask, float maxDistance, out NavMeshHit hit)

docs.summary:
How far along its current path the agent could get, without moving it: walks the path from where the agent stands and stops at `maxDistance`, at the end of the path, or where the path first enters a polygon `areaMask` excludes.

True when the walk stopped short of `maxDistance`. Two different things cause that, and the mask tells them apart: `!hit.Mask.Overlaps(areaMask)` means an excluded polygon blocked it, anything else means the path simply ran out. `hit.Hit` separately says the position is a real point on the path rather than one interpolated where the budget ran out, and `hit.Distance` is measured ALONG the path rather than to it.

Mid-hop across an off-mesh link the corridor already begins at the landing point, so the walk is measured from there rather than from where the agent hangs.

Areas are tested per POLYGON rather than per corner, so a path that only clips the corner of an excluded polygon still stops at it.
Called every frame after all Update functions have been called.

The agent's steering envelope: the crowd treats an agent as an upright cylinder of [`Radius`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~Radius) x [`Height`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~Height) standing on the navmesh, so that is what is drawn — sized and placed exactly as the simulation sees it, including [`BaseOffset`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~BaseOffset). Drawn unselected (like colliders) so a whole crowd's footprints are visible while tuning.

The route the agent is currently steering along, plus its destination — drawn from the crowd's own corner list, so it shows what the simulation is actually following rather than a re-planned guess. Only meaningful while a crowd is running (in the editor an unregistered agent has no path).
